You review a Rust program against a numbered requirement document.
For each requirement Rn, decide whether the program satisfies it on the intended
concurrency semantics: answer yes, no, or unsure, and cite the Rust line(s) that
justify your answer. Also decide whether the program contains a concurrency bug
(deadlock, lost wakeup, race, busy-wait, missing release, ...): yes, no, or
unsure, with the offending line. Do not assume the program is correct.
Output only a JSON object:
{"bug_present": "yes|no|unsure", "bug_evidence": "<line refs or ->",
 "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "yes|no|unsure", "line": "<refs>"}, ...}}

content: {"bug_present": "no", "bug_evidence": "-", "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "main: thread::spawn(move || w1(s1)); thread::spawn(move || w2(s2));"}, "R2": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "w1/w2: let mut guard = shared.lock().unwrap(); compute(); ... guard.acc = tmp2;"}, "R3": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "w1/w2: guard dropped at end of inner block before function returns"}, "R4": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "Mutex<Shared> ensures mutual exclusion"}, "R5": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "shared.lock().unwrap() blocks until available"}, "R6": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "no loops or blocking cycles; both threads terminate"}, "R7": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "h1.join().unwrap(); h2.join().unwrap();"}, "R8": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "println!(\"DONE done={}\", done); with acc incremented twice from 0"}}}
